objective: Provide provider-neutral multi-window budget, token, concurrency, reservation, settlement, release, and overrun controls for model routing without contacting providers or treating model/runtime metadata as authority.

research_inputs.finding: Current vLLM documentation describes experimental prefill/decode disaggregation, KV-cache transfer connectors, and independent TTFT/ITL tuning while explicitly noting that disaggregation alone does not improve throughput.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Runtime/cache facts remain caller-supplied route evidence; the budget contract does not infer performance or authority from provider claims.

research_inputs.finding: LiteLLM documents provider-agnostic MCP gateway routing, key/team permissions, multiple transports, OAuth, end-user tracking, and explicit tool approval behavior.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Route budget, tool authorization, credentials, and model execution remain separate control-plane decisions.

research_inputs.finding: Current budget documentation describes multi-window cost limits, token/request rate limits, concurrency, agent/session caps, fallbacks, and fail-closed enforcement when authoritative spend cannot be verified.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds bounded local reservation and settlement with multi-window capacity and overrun rejection, without importing a provider gateway.

research_inputs.finding: SGLang documents prefix/radix caching, zero-overhead scheduling, disaggregation, speculative decoding, continuous batching, structured outputs, and heterogeneous hardware support.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Cache and runtime characteristics are kept as route evidence and never become privilege, correctness, or execution authority.

features: explicit release path that returns reservation capacity
nonce replay protection and full reservation-body tamper detection

limitations: The ledger is a bounded userspace/control-plane primitive and does not contact model providers, invoke inference engines, execute tools, or enforce budgets across distributed nodes.
Cost, token, concurrency, route, generation, and time values are caller-supplied evidence; this local implementation does not independently attest provider billing or usage.
Settlement rejects usage over the reservation rather than claiming it can undo external provider consumption; an external supervisor must handle provider-side reconciliation.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes network, storage, provider, model, accelerator, and kernel latency.
The snapshot-index adjacent regression was not claimed as passed because its bounded run timed out after earlier successful markers; the other ten adjacent suites passed.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, superiority to Linux, or resolution of existing external release blockers.
